Harlan saw it from the gallery, sixty feet above the breakers, and climbed down the iron stairs with hands still smelling of lamp oil. The cork crumbled when he pulled it. Inside, a single sheet of paper, soft as cloth from months at sea. The handwriting was small and steady: coordinates, a date eight months past, and one line—'Still here. Lantern visible. Thank you.' He read it twice, then looked out at the horizon as if someone might still be watching. No vessel. No signal. Only the endless grey swells and the gulls wheeling beneath the beam that he kept burning every night without knowing whether it mattered. Now he knew.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市褪去霓虹的外衣，露出灰蓝色的素颜。街灯仍亮着，光晕落在空旷的柏油路上，像一枚枚安静的铜币。环卫工人的扫帚划过人行道，沙沙声在楼宇间回荡，惊起一只栖息在变压器上的野猫。早点铺的蒸笼刚刚架上灶台，白色的水汽从半卷的铁帘下溢出，裹着面粉与葱花的气息。出租车亮着空车灯缓缓驶过十字路口，红绿灯兀自变换，忠实地指挥着并不存在的车流。远处工地的塔吊悬着一盏孤灯，混凝土的气味随夜风飘散。整座城市像一个翻了个身尚未醒来的人，呼吸均匀而绵长。", "w03": "• Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of the same problem—like looking up a word in a dictionary and finding the definition uses another word you also need to look up.\n• Every recursive function needs a \"base case\"—a simple version of the problem it can answer immediately without calling itself again, so it doesn't keep going forever.\n• Think of Russian nesting dolls: you open one and find a smaller one inside, and you keep opening until you reach the tiniest doll that doesn't open—that tiny doll is the base case."}
